feature: A filled shape looks filled on the canvas
summary: A circle you fill with a colour now looks filled while you work on it, at every zoom and every document size. It used to come out as a hollow ring on the canvas on about half of them, while the picture the app exported, the layers panel thumbnail and the icon previews beside it all had it solid.
setup: Photonz Dev, any release. Nothing to switch on: this is the renderer everything draws through.

try.do: Open a new document 1600 by 1100. It opens at 75%, which is the zoom this went wrong at.
Press F and drag out a frame in the middle of it.
Press E and drag out a circle inside that frame.
Check the circle is solid red, not a red outline with white inside.
Compare it with its row in the Layers panel: the thumbnail is solid too, and used to be the only one that was.
Look at the five icon preview chips in the top left: 16 through 64 are all solid discs.
Do the same in a 1100 by 700 document and a 2400 by 1700 one, one circle inside a frame and one loose beside it.

evaluate: At 75% on a 1600 by 1100 document, is the circle solid?
Does the circle on the canvas match its thumbnail in the Layers panel at every zoom you try?
In an icon frame, do the five preview chips agree with the canvas now?
Is there any other shape or size where the canvas still disagrees with what Export writes?
rough: The canvas was the one lying, not the export: the document always said filled, and the fix is in a silhouette the renderer bakes rather than in anything the document holds. Nothing on disk changes and no saved file needs anything done to it.

The same arithmetic drew a ring with a hole punched in it for any border at least half as thick as the shape is narrow. That is fixed by the same change and covered by a test, but the Border Width slider stops at 40, so you can only see it on a shape smaller than 80 points across.

Left rough on purpose: the baked silhouette is rounded to whole pixels, so on a box whose size is fractional it can be up to a pixel wider than the box it stands for. The pixel-sharing arithmetic clamps that away, so nothing shows on screen, but it is a smell in the same function.
